November 18, 2026
JAKARTA – Organizers were forced to cut short the 2026 Borobudur Marathon in Central Java before its scheduled finish on Sunday after extreme heat raised concerns over runners’ safety, with hundreds reportedly falling ill.
Race Director Andreas Kansil said organizers halted the race at 9:45 a.m. local time after monitoring showed the Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) had reached 32.3 degrees Celsius, triggering a black-flag warning for extreme heat.
The WBGT is a composite heat-stress index that measures the effects of environmental conditions on the human body. It takes into account air temperature, humidity, wind speed and solar radiation and is used to assess the risk of heat-related illness during outdoor activities.
“The conditions posed a risk of heat-related illnesses, including heatstroke,” Kansil said on Sunday as quoted by Kompas.id.
“Conditions were even hotter along kilometers 32 to 34, where the last runners were on the course. With our medical tents already at 90 percent capacity and more runners potentially needing medical assistance, we decided to stop the race to protect participants’ safety,” he added.
The marathon was halted with 1 hour and 15 minutes remaining before the 11 a.m. cutoff time, with about 2,000 runners still on the course out of 5,000 registered participants in the category. The other two race categories had already concluded, with the half-marathon finishing at 8:50 a.m. and the 10-kilometer race at 7:40 a.m.
This was the second time in the event’s 10-year history that organizers had been forced to halt the race. The previous stoppage occurred in 2023, also because of extreme heat.
Andreas said that after the race was halted, organizers began locating runners still on the course and arranging for them to be transported to the finish line, particularly those at the back of the field.
“All participants who are taken to the finish line will receive finisher medals. What matters most to us is the safety of every runner,” Andreas said.
Borobudur Marathon 2026 Medical Director Wawan Budisusilo said the event’s medical personnel, numbering around 400, were overwhelmed by the number of runners seeking treatment, prompting organizers to consult with the race director and technical delegates from World Athletics before agreeing to halt the race.
“We discussed the situation with the race director and World Athletics technical delegates and agreed to stop the race,” Wawan said.
Organizers said 244 runners had received medical treatment at the event’s medical tents by the time the race was halted. Medical teams reported cases of heatstroke, heat exhaustion and one case of cardiac arrest.
The runner who suffered cardiac arrest was successfully resuscitated through cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and taken to hospital, organizers said.
The Borobudur Marathon is one of Indonesia’s largest and most popular running events. It is organized through a partnership between the Central Java administration, its regional development bank Bank Jateng, the Borobudur Marathon Foundation and Kompas daily newspaper.
The race takes runners along routes surrounding Borobudur temple, the world’s largest Buddhist temple, through the scenic rural landscapes of Magelang regency.
This year’s event attracted 12,500 runners from 38 countries, up from 11,500 participants last year.
